source_facts.capacity_path: When observe() sees a non-matching learnable pattern at len(candidates) >= max_candidates, it calls prune(time_ms); if still at capacity, observe() returns None and does not create a new candidate.
source_facts.prune_path: prune() removes only candidates whose episode_count <= immature_stale_episodes and whose last_seen age exceeds stale_after_ms.
source_facts.reason_default_mature_reclamation_false: Default maturity is episode_count >= 3 while default stale-prune eligibility requires episode_count <= 2; no other v0.5 source path found that evicts, compacts, ages out, or replaces mature candidates.
source_facts.default_brain_config: IntegratedV05Brain accepts optional assembly_config but otherwise constructs TemporalAssemblyMemory(AssemblyConfig()).
source_facts.checkpoint_behavior: state_dict serializes all candidates/config/next_id/suppressed; load_checkpoint restores TemporalAssemblyMemory.from_state_dict(). No source-level lifecycle meaning is attached to persistence.
source_facts.pattern_multiplicity_per_episode: patterns_from_step may produce one pattern per cascade and therefore the static source does not give a one-candidate-per-episode upper bound.

AssemblyConfig.test_override: tests/v05/test_v05_assemblies.py overrides mature_episodes only; it does not set max_candidates.

docs/V05_MASTER_PLAN.md: Assembly Layer design language includes candidate formation, recurrence tracking, selectivity evaluation, and stability / decay.
The Assembly-candidate proliferation risk section lists null false-positive gate, candidate decay, minimum recurrence, candidate budget, and matched-noise calibration as mitigations.
The plan does not define max_candidates as a lifetime cap, active working set, or cache and does not specify mature-candidate reclamation semantics.
Checkpoint/replay is described as reproducibility/integration behavior, not as a promise that candidate persistence is permanent lifecycle policy.
docs/THEORY_SPEC_v0.5.md: Assembly Candidate is an unlabeled recurring spatiotemporal Cascade cluster.
A candidate must satisfy preregistered recurrence, episode, stability, and false-positive conditions before being accepted.
Candidate-count proliferation under null noise is a failure condition.
No lifetime-cap, working-set, cache, mature-eviction, or post-saturation acquisition contract is stated.
docs/V05_EXPERIMENT_PROTOCOL.md: Development seeds are 501 and 502; training episodes per seed are 48; held-out episodes per condition per seed are 16.
Secondary plasticity-ablation training episodes are 24 and held-out episodes are 8.
Gate B constrains mean mature candidates learned from null noise to at most 1.0.
The protocol does not state a saturation target, post-saturation learning requirement, or max_candidates lifecycle contract.
docs/V05_CLAIM_BOUNDARIES.md: Permitted engineering claim includes clustering unlabeled Cascade observations into Assembly Candidates.
No lifecycle or capacity semantics are declared.

tests/v05/test_v05_assemblies.py: Tests maturation only across distinct episodes.
Tests suppression and state round-trip preserving episode lineage.
Contains no max_candidates, saturation, mature reclamation, capacity turnover, or post-saturation novel-acquisition assertion.

caller_and_horizon_facts.null_train_learning_horizon: uses the provided count; run_seed supplies train_count, default 48
caller_and_horizon_facts.why_saturation_not_structurally_preclude: The learning horizon is bounded, but patterns_from_step can yield multiple Assembly patterns per episode and no stable supported contract proves a candidate upper bound below 256.
caller_and_horizon_facts.why_saturation_not_structurally_establis: No stable supported default caller overrides max_candidates=256, no supported test constructs capacity saturation, and no supported doc/caller promises continued novel-pattern acquisition after saturation.
